answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake in a shared bond before it may transact, with the stake slashed if peers prove fraud. A newcomer starts in a probationary haven with tiny limits, earning trust only through a plume of verified, useful work over time. No agent can forge that history cheaply, since each fake identity must post its own stake and wait out the same probation. Creating ten thousand sock puppets then costs ten thousand stakes and months of real work, while honest agents keep their bond and graduate to full limits.
